introH2: 🏔️ How many kinds of mountain-view stays are on Chanthaburi's Soi Dao–Khao Khitchakut side, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: When people think of Chanthaburi, many picture Chao Lao beach and the riverside community in town first. But the eastern side of the province — around Makham, Pong Nam Ron and Soi Dao districts — is the mountain zone: cool air, morning mist, orchards covering the hillsides, all within driving distance of Khao Khitchakut. So stays here mostly play on "mountain views and quiet." Some are budget-friendly streamside homestays near Khao Khitchakut, some are brand-standard golf resorts at the foot of Soi Dao, some are orchard resorts where you wake up to a sea of mist, and some are houses up in the hills you can book whole with friends. These differences are why people who book the wrong style feel it doesn't match their trip — say, you wanted a pool but ended up at a simple nature stay, or you wanted to walk to a restaurant but ended up deep in an orchard. This article rounds up 5 mountain-view stays on the Soi Dao–Khao Khitchakut side that we've already reviewed in depth. Every one comes from reading real guest reviews, telling you the upsides and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites and giving you direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: All 5 stays are in the mountain zone on Chanthaburi's eastern side, with no convenient public transport running through. The single most important thing they share is that you should have your own car everywhere and fill up the tank before heading up. The areas in this article: Makham district — semi-mountain orchards along streams, near Khao Khitchakut and Phlio Waterfall, home to Akantuka, the homestays and Our Eco Farm. Pong Nam Ron district (Thap Sai subdistrict) — the foot of Soi Dao: cool air, mist, orchards and a golf course, home to Chatrium Golf Resort, The Natural Garden Resort and Check in Phureeya Ville. From Chanthaburi town to these areas is about 35–50 km, roughly a 40-minute to 1-hour drive. Popular places to head on to are Khao Khitchakut, Soi Dao Waterfall, Phlio Waterfall and the seasonal orchards.

entries.storyHtml: If you want to start with the most budget-friendly nature-view stay on the Khao Khitchakut side in this set, plenty of reviews mention Akantuka Homestay. It's a family-run stay in Chaman subdistrict, Makham district, on the semi-mountain eastern side of Chanthaburi, within driving distance of the Buddha's Footprint shrine at Khao Khitchakut and Phlio Waterfall. What sets it apart from a typical stay is that the property sits right beside a clear stream that flows all year round, which becomes the view, the place to hang out and a spot to cool off in all at once. There are around 30 rooms and villas spread across the garden grounds, from a Standard from about ฿912 with breakfast for two, a Suite from about ฿1,368, up to a Villa that sleeps several from about ฿2,780 with breakfast for four — very reasonable prices for the setting you get. Facilities are complete for this style of stay: a swimming pool, restaurant, karaoke room, banquet room, activity areas and gardens, free parking and Wi-Fi in the common areas, plus CCTV throughout. On Booking.com the score sits around 8.2, and real reviews praise the clear stream, good service, the pool and the quiet atmosphere. Honest caveats from the reviews: the location is deep in the grounds so you need your own car, there are no convenience stores within walking distance, and a few reviews note cleanliness issues in some rooms, like dust or gecko droppings in corners that aren't used much. This isn't a luxury resort, but it's a streamside homestay that gives you nature and quiet at the lowest price in these five — good for families and groups of friends who want to visit Khao Khitchakut and stay right by the water.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're coming as a group, pick the Villa Room — it includes breakfast for four and sleeps several, so the per-person cost works out better. Fill up the tank and buy food to bring along before entering the grounds, because shops are hard to find nearby; and if you plan to climb Khao Khitchakut during the pilgrimage-season opening, check the dates and book your stay ahead.

entries.storyHtml: Among the mountain-view stays on the Soi Dao side, if you measure by hotel standard and review count, Chatrium Golf Resort Soi Dao Chanthaburi is the most polished in this set — a 4-star golf resort under Chatrium Hotels & Residences at the foot of Soi Dao, in Thap Sai subdistrict, Pong Nam Ron district. It scores 4.6 from 259 reviews on TripAdvisor and ranks #1 among stays in the Thap Sai area. Its heart is an 18-hole championship course designed by Denis Griffiths across more than 1,580 acres, with mountains as the backdrop the whole way round; many golfers' reviews rate it one of the most scenic courses in the east. There are around 47 recently renovated rooms, starting with the Deluxe Mountain View at 40 sqm for about ฿2,550 — larger than the standard room at a typical resort — with every room facing the mountains or the golf course, up to the Soi Dao Mountain View Suite at 80 sqm. There's an outdoor pool with a kids' pool and a Pool Bar, a Thai-massage spa, and the Soi Dao Restaurant, which reviews praise for good food and lovely course views, especially at breakfast when you can see mist drifting over the fairways. An important thing to know, per reviews and the resort's own notice: the golf course is under renovation from March to October 2026, partly open, so anyone coming specifically to play should always check the course's status before booking. Honest caveats from the reviews: the location is about 46 km from town so you need your own car, dining options outside the resort are so limited that nearly every meal ends up being eaten on site, some corners are decorated in a classic style that shows the building's age, and caddies fluent in English are limited. Best for golfers, families and anyone who wants a brand-standard mountain-view resort with full facilities all in one place.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're coming to play golf, call to check the course status before booking since it's under renovation in 2026, and there are golf packages from about ฿3,700/night that work out better than booking separately. Ask for a floor with a clear view of the mountain range or the golf course for the morning view, and plan your meals because restaurants outside the resort are hard to find.

entries.storyHtml: The Natural Garden Resort is a resort the owners developed from their family's fruit orchard on a Soi Dao hillside into a stay surrounded by nature, in Thap Sai subdistrict, Pong Nam Ron district. What guests talk about most is the Soi Dao mountain views that are lovely both morning and evening, and the chance to catch a sea of mist in the early mornings of the cool season, ringed by tens of rai of durian, longan, mango, mangosteen and tamarind orchards. The charm here lies in the variety of accommodation: from a Deluxe with balcony at about ฿1,500, a Deluxe Mountain View facing the range, separate garden villas in the orchard, a Pool Villa of about 40 sqm that's the best room, to a glamping camping zone with comfortable beds and electricity for those who want to sleep in the mountain breeze on a budget. There's a multi-depth outdoor pool that reviews say kids can play in all day, a garden cafe with a fire pit for cool evenings, and a meeting room for seminar groups and team-building. On Trip.com it scores 8.8 (cleanliness 9.3, service 9.2), and on TripAdvisor 4.1/5, ranking #1 among B&B-type stays in Thap Sai, with location scoring as high as 4.5 and value 4.3. Honest caveats from the reviews: it's far out so you need your own car and should fill up first, some rooms' beds are fairly firm and the air-con is noisy in certain rooms, English signage and information are limited, and the garden lights are fairly bright so stargazing isn't at its best. Best for families, groups of friends and couples who want to relax with mountain views in an orchard setting at a slow pace over several nights.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want the full view, specify a room or villa facing the range when you book. Come in the cool season (Nov–Feb) for the best chance of a morning sea of mist, and if you want to taste fresh orchard fruit, May–Jul is the eastern fruit season. Coming as a group, try booking a whole villa or the camping zone — the per-person cost works out better.

entries.storyHtml: Check in Phureeya Ville, which locals call Phureeya Ville, is a small house-style resort up in the hills in Thap Sai subdistrict, Pong Nam Ron district, that sells atmosphere and privacy more than luxury. It's a stay of around 8 villa-style houses spread across the grounds, holding about 30 guests when full. What sets it apart is that each house has a balcony or terrace where you can sit and look out at the mountains ringing you in 360 degrees, amid the mist and comfortably cool air almost year-round in the Pong Nam Ron area. Real reviews say the people it suits are couples who want a quiet stay, families and groups of friends who want to book a whole house and sit around chatting in the cool air. There's an on-site restaurant and cafe whose selling point is coffee amid the mountain views, making a morning coffee on the balcony the activity many guests love most; there's a 24-hour reception, free parking, and pets are allowed at no extra charge. The overall score is 8.3 from 61 reviews, which is good for a small stay in a remote area. Honest caveats from the reviews: it's about 35–40 km from town, the final stretch up the hill is winding so you should drive yourself and take care at night, there's no pool, the facilities are simple in the manner of an upcountry resort, internet and mobile signal may not be as strong as in town, and how new each house feels can vary. Best for anyone who wants to escape the city to stay up in the hills, quiet and private, on an affordable budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's a small stay that isn't listed on every platform, so for the most accurate prices and availability you should check directly with the property by phone or Line, especially in the cool season and on long weekends. Coming as a group, try booking the whole two-storey house for better value, and bring a warm jacket because the mountain air is much cooler than in town at night.
pros: 360-degree mountain views and morning mist, comfortably cool air almost year-round
Separate houses, private, good for couples, families and whole-house groups
On-site restaurant and cafe, good coffee, free parking
Pets allowed at no extra charge
cons: Far from town, with a winding final stretch up the hill — you should drive yourself

entries.storyHtml: Closing out this set is the quietest stay of all — Our Eco Farm (Baan Eco Farm), a small farmstay tucked into a streamside farm garden in Ban Pong Rong Sen, Patthawi subdistrict, Makham district, on the same semi-mountain eastern side of Chanthaburi as Akantuka. What sets it apart from a typical stay is that it doesn't sell the sea or fancy design — it sells being a farm and being nature, just as the name says. It's a stay in the middle of a garden, lots of trees, a stream running through, so quiet that many guests say they hear only the water and the birds. There are only around 13 rooms, split into Standard and Superior with queen beds; every room has air-con and a private garden-view balcony, from about ฿1,000 in normal periods. What earns the highest praise is the service, which scores around 9.8 on Trip.com — reviews say the owners and staff are warm and look after you like family, and speak several languages: Thai, English, German and Dutch, with freshly made breakfasts many guests praise. It's a stay that allows pets, and there are farm dogs and cats many reviews mention fondly, plus a stream to swim in, BBQ and fishing. Real review scores are high at around 9.5 from 11 reviews on Trip.com and 8.2 from 267 reviews on Agoda. Honest caveats from the reviews: the location is deep in the grounds, the entrance is fairly isolated and dark at night so you should drive yourself and return before dark, there are no shops within walking distance, there's no pool, and it's a small farm without staff on duty 24 hours. Best for couples, animal lovers and anyone who wants to escape the bustle to stay quietly with streamside nature at one of the lowest prices in this set.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Drive yourself and plan to get back before dark, because the entrance is dark and isolated. Bring food along or have the farm kitchen handle your meals, since there are no shops around, and if you're bringing dogs or cats let them know in advance when booking. There are only around 13 rooms, which fill up fast in the cool season and fruit season, so book ahead.
pros: A streamside farm in a garden, quiet enough to hear the water, comfortably cool air

faqTitle: FAQ — questions travelers often ask about mountain-view stays on Chanthaburi's Soi Dao–Khao Khitchakut side

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best mountain-view stay on the Soi Dao–Khao Khitchakut side?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. If you want to stay by a stream near Khao Khitchakut on a budget, Akantuka Homestay from ฿912 has a pool and includes breakfast. If you want a brand standard and a golf course, Chatrium Golf Resort Soi Dao scores TripAdvisor 4.6, #1 in Thap Sai. If you want to catch a sea of mist in an orchard, The Natural Garden Resort. If you want to book a whole house with 360-degree views, Check in Phureeya Ville. And if you want the quietest spot close to nature, Our Eco Farm, whose service scores around 9.8.

faq.q: ❓ How much do mountain-view stays on the Soi Dao side cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at about ฿912–2,550 per night. At the budget end are Akantuka Homestay from ฿912, Our Eco Farm ฿1,000, Check in Phureeya Ville ฿1,200 and The Natural Garden Resort ฿1,500. At the top is Chatrium Golf Resort Soi Dao from ฿2,550 (the 80 sqm suite up to about ฿5,500). All prices are approximate starting prices from the standard room; during festivals and the cool season prices may run higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Do I need my own car to stay in the Soi Dao–Pong Nam Ron–Makham zone?
faq.a: You should. All 5 stays are in the mountain zone on Chanthaburi's eastern side, about 35–50 km from town, with no convenient public transport running through and no convenience stores within walking distance. At some, like Our Eco Farm and Check in Phureeya Ville, the final stretch up the hill and at night is fairly dark, so you should drive yourself, fill up the tank, and allow extra time if you arrive late. Some offer pickup (at extra charge) — ask in advance.

faq.q: ❓ How close are stays in this zone to Khao Khitchakut and the waterfalls?
faq.a: They're within day-trip driving distance. Akantuka Homestay and Our Eco Farm in Makham district are within driving range of Khao Khitchakut and Phlio Waterfall. On the other side, Chatrium Golf Resort, The Natural Garden Resort and Check in Phureeya Ville in Thap Sai, Pong Nam Ron are near Soi Dao, Soi Dao Waterfall and the golf course. From any of them you can drive on to the sights in not much time, making them good bases for nature trips in the east.

faq.q: ❓ Which Soi Dao-zone stay suits pets and families?
faq.a: The ones that clearly take pets are Our Eco Farm (which even has farm dogs and cats) and Check in Phureeya Ville, where they're welcome at no extra charge. For families who want wide space for kids to run around plus a pool, The Natural Garden Resort and Chatrium Golf Resort Soi Dao fit that need for pool and space, while Akantuka Homestay has both a pool and a stream for kids to swim.

faq.q: ❓ When's the best time to stay at a mountain-view spot on the Soi Dao side?
faq.a: The most beautiful time is the cool season (November–February): cool air and the best chance of a morning sea of mist, especially at The Natural Garden Resort and Check in Phureeya Ville. It's high season, rooms fill up fast, so book ahead. If you want to taste fresh orchard fruit like durian, May–July is the eastern fruit season, though there may be some rain. Every platform usually offers Free Cancellation — we recommend locking in that kind of rate first if your plans aren't set, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
